proof_spine: define subgroup and normal-subgroup properties over the existing group setting
show the native kernel set builder contains the identity and is closed under multiplication and inverse
show every conjugate of a kernel element maps to the target identity

setting GroupSetting(A nonempty_set, mul fn(x, y A) A, one A, inv fn(x A) A):
    forall u, v, w A:
        mul(mul(u, v), w) = mul(u, mul(v, w))
    forall u A:
        mul(one, u) = u
        mul(u, one) = u
        mul(inv(u), u) = one
        mul(u, inv(u)) = one
blocks.reusable_lesson: The parameterized setting is the single reusable group-law bundle.

blocks.intent: Replay the existing definition-facing group predicate.
blocks.reusable_lesson: The proposition reuses the same setting bundle without duplicating laws.

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm group_left_cancel:
    ? forall [GroupSetting], a, b, c A:
        mul(a, b) = mul(a, c)
        =>:
            b = c
    mul(inv(a), a) = one
    b = mul(one, b) = mul(mul(inv(a), a), b) = mul(inv(a), mul(a, b)) = mul(inv(a), mul(a, c)) = mul(mul(inv(a), a), c) = mul(one, c) = c
blocks.reusable_lesson: Cancellation remains available to the homomorphism toolkit.

blocks.intent: Replay uniqueness of the group identity.
blocks.accepted_litex:
thm group_identity_unique:
    ? forall [GroupSetting], identity A:
        forall a A:
            mul(identity, a) = a
            mul(a, identity) = a
        =>:
            identity = one
    identity = mul(one, identity) = one
blocks.reusable_lesson: Identity uniqueness is part of the established group toolkit.

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm group_inverse_unique:
    ? forall [GroupSetting], a, b A:
        mul(b, a) = one
        =>:
            b = inv(a)
    mul(a, inv(a)) = one
    b = mul(b, one) = mul(b, mul(a, inv(a))) = mul(mul(b, a), inv(a)) = mul(one, inv(a)) = inv(a)
blocks.reusable_lesson: Inverse uniqueness later identifies the inverse of the target identity.

blocks.accepted_litex:
prop is_group_homomorphism([GroupSetting(A, mul_A, one_A, inv_A)], [GroupSetting(B, mul_B, one_B, inv_B)], f fn(x A) B):
    forall x, y A:
        f(mul_A(x, y)) = mul_B(f(x), f(y))
blocks.reusable_lesson: The homomorphism predicate composes two existing group bundles.

blocks.accepted_litex:
setting GroupHomomorphismSetting([GroupSetting(A, mul_A, one_A, inv_A)], [GroupSetting(B, mul_B, one_B, inv_B)], f fn(x A) B):
    forall x, y A:
        f(mul_A(x, y)) = mul_B(f(x), f(y))
blocks.reusable_lesson: The flagship theorem can quantify over this single composed setting.

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm homomorphism_maps_identity:
    ? forall [GroupHomomorphismSetting]:
        f(one_A) = one_B
    mul_A(one_A, one_A) = one_A
    mul_B(f(one_A), f(one_A)) = f(mul_A(one_A, one_A)) = f(one_A) = mul_B(f(one_A), one_B)
    by thm group_left_cancel(B, mul_B, one_B, inv_B, f(one_A), f(one_A), one_B)
blocks.reusable_lesson: Identity preservation proves the kernel contains the source identity.

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm homomorphism_maps_inverse:
    ? forall [GroupHomomorphismSetting], a A:
        f(inv_A(a)) = inv_B(f(a))
    by thm homomorphism_maps_identity(A, mul_A, one_A, inv_A, B, mul_B, one_B, inv_B, f)
    mul_A(inv_A(a), a) = one_A
    mul_B(f(inv_A(a)), f(a)) = f(mul_A(inv_A(a), a)) = f(one_A) = one_B
    by thm group_inverse_unique(B, mul_B, one_B, inv_B, f(a), f(inv_A(a)))
blocks.reusable_lesson: Inverse preservation proves kernel closure under source inverses.

        by thm set_builder_member(one_A, {candidate A: f(candidate) = one_B})
        claim:
            ? forall kernel_x, kernel_y {candidate A: f(candidate) = one_B}:
                mul_A(kernel_x, kernel_y) $in {candidate A: f(candidate) = one_B}
            f(kernel_x) = one_B
            f(kernel_y) = one_B
            f(mul_A(kernel_x, kernel_y)) = mul_B(f(kernel_x), f(kernel_y)) = mul_B(one_B, one_B) = one_B

            ? forall kernel_x {candidate A: f(candidate) = one_B}:
                inv_A(kernel_x) $in {candidate A: f(candidate) = one_B}
            f(kernel_x) = one_B
            by thm homomorphism_maps_inverse(A, mul_A, one_A, inv_A, B, mul_B, one_B, inv_B, f, kernel_x)

            f(inv_A(kernel_x)) = inv_B(f(kernel_x)) = inv_B(one_B) = one_B
            by thm set_builder_member(inv_A(kernel_x), {candidate A: f(candidate) = one_B})

    claim:

        mul_B(f(conjugator), one_B) = f(conjugator)
        f(mul_A(mul_A(conjugator, kernel_h), inv_A(conjugator))) = mul_B(f(mul_A(conjugator, kernel_h)), f(inv_A(conjugator))) = mul_B(mul_B(f(conjugator), f(kernel_h)), inv_B(f(conjugator))) = mul_B(mul_B(f(conjugator), one_B), inv_B(f(conjugator))) = mul_B(f(conjugator), inv_B(f(conjugator))) = one_B
        by thm set_builder_member(mul_A(mul_A(conjugator, kernel_h), inv_A(conjugator)), {candidate A: f(candidate) = one_B})
    by def $is_normal_subgroup(A, mul_A, one_A, inv_A, {candidate A: f(candidate) = one_B})
